  "stim_paradigms_compared": [

    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The substantial mean differences across paradigms (Sham: 4.68s vs Combined: 2.56s) suggest strong paradigm effects.",
    "For Success: Logistic regression or generalized linear mixed model with binomial family, NOT standard ANOVA. Success is binary (0/1) with mean 0.73, violating normality and homoscedasticity assumptions required for ANOVA. Use binomial GLM with logit link, or arcsine transformation with caution if linear probability model insisted.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Extreme right-skew evident (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) with near-zero minimum; log-transformation strongly advised. Paradigm means range from 0.31 (Sham) to 0.50 (Bright Visual Only), suggesting meaningful differences.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Distribution appears more symmetric (mean=12.50, sd=4.46, max=75.35) but with some high outliers; check diagnostics. Paradigm means are relatively compressed (10.74 to 12.83 cm/s).",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1] variable with mean 0.38, sd 0.24; beta regression may be more appropriate given bounds, but ANOVA with arcsine-square-root transformation is defensible. Clear paradigm gradient: Sham (0.236) < Dim Visual (0.336) < ICMS Only (0.354) < Bright Visual (0.387) < Combined (0.399)."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures structure—8 mice with unequal trial counts (SC21LM: 10986 trials, SC11LM: 7233 trials). Mouse must be included as random effect or cluster-robust standard errors used.",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests required for each response by paradigm. Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency severely non-normal; AD bounded; Success binary.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms. Unequal n (Combined: 48846 vs Sham: 3505) reduces power for variance comparison; Welch's ANOVA or robust methods if variances differ.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (63.7% of data), creating precision imbalance. Weighted analyses or mixed models with appropriate variance structures recommended.",
    "Outlier assessment: Extreme values in Time-to-Target (201.39s), Path Efficiency (29.82), and Average Speed (75.35 cm/s) require investigation; winsorization or robust methods if influential."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA/GLM significant: Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for continuous responses (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD), with adjustment for unequal sample sizes using Tukey-Kramer.",
    "For Success (binomial GLM): Estimated marginal means with z-tests, Bonferroni or FDR correction for 10 pairwise comparisons across 5 paradigms.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs all unimodal paradigms (multisensory enhancement hypothesis); Sham vs all active stimulation (baseline performance); Visual-only (Dim vs Bright) vs ICMS Only (modality comparison).",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables (with correction for unequal n), odds ratios for Success, and confidence intervals for all comparisons.",
    "Multiplicity control: Family-wise error rate controlled at α=0.05 across 5 response variables using Bonferroni (α=0.01 per variable) or hierarchical testing."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Success (27.3%), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31), lowest Average Speed (10.74 cm/s), and lowest AD (0.236).",
    "Combined paradigm expected to show best or near-best performance: lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Success (78.0%), high Path Efficiency (0.50), highest Average Speed (12.83 cm/s), and highest AD (0.399), consistent with multisensory integration benefits.",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only expected intermediate and similar: Success ~68-67%, Time-to-Target ~3.05-3.14s, Path Efficiency ~0.43, suggesting comparable unimodal efficacy.",
    "Bright Visual Only unexpectedly strong: Success (78.5%) and Path Efficiency (0.50) comparable to Combined, with lowest Time-to-Target among unimodal conditions (2.61s), suggesting visual salience may match multisensory benefit for some metrics.",
    "AD gradient expected to parallel performance: higher angular dispersion associated with better performance paradigms, possibly reflecting more exploratory or directed search patterns."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in paradigm representation: Combined (63.7%) vs Sham (4.6%) and Bright Visual Only (4.3%) limits precision for rare paradigms and may bias variance estimates.",
    "Mouse-level clustering ignored in standard ANOVA: 8 mice with 7233-10986 trials each violate independence assumption; mouse identity confounded with paradigm if assignment non-random.",
    "Cross-sectional summary data only: No temporal dynamics, learning curves, or trial-level covariates (e.g., target location, difficulty) available for adjustment.",
    "Binary Success outcome inappropriate for ANOVA: Requires binomial GLM, but summary statistics provided are means (probabilities), not raw counts or variance structures.",
    "Path Efficiency extreme values suggest measurement artifacts or rare events (max=29.82) that may distort parametric analyses.",
    "No information on experimental design: Randomization, counterbalancing, or block structure unknown; potential confounding by run order or session effects."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMM) for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept; fit generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family for Success. Use restricted maximum likelihood (REML) for LMMs, Laplace approximation or adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for GLMM. Apply Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom and Satterthwaite approximation for inference. Conduct likelihood ratio tests for paradigm effects, followed by estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment. If computational constraints prevent mixed models, use cluster-robust standard errors by Mouse with HC3 correction. For Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target, evaluate log-transformation versus gamma GLMM with log link given right-skew. Report intra-class correlation (ICC) to quantify mouse-level clustering importance."
}
